glossary.Circulating volume: The amount of blood in the vessels, which keeps organs perfused.
glossary.Electrolyte: A salt in the blood, such as sodium or potassium.
glossary.Electrolytes: Salts in the blood such as sodium and potassium.
glossary.Diarrhoea: Loose or watery stools passed more often than normal.
glossary.Diabetes: High blood glucose from lack of insulin or insulin resistance.
glossary.Dry mucous membranes: A dry mouth and tongue, a sign of fluid loss.
glossary.Sunken eyes: Eyes that look hollow from fluid loss in the tissues around them.
glossary.Shock: Inadequate blood flow to the tissues, causing organ failure.
glossary.Confusion: Muddled thinking and poor attention, here from poor brain perfusion.
glossary.Clinical assessment: Diagnosis from history and examination rather than tests.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate way of making a diagnosis.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells, platelets and haematocrit.
glossary.Blood glucose: Sugar level in the blood, checked to find diabetes as a cause.
glossary.Sodium: Main salt in blood; rises when more water than salt is lost.
glossary.Potassium: Salt mainly inside cells; abnormal levels can cause heart rhythm problems.
glossary.Saline: Salt water solution given IV; 0.9% matches blood salt concentration.
glossary.Oedema: Swelling from fluid leaking into tissues.
glossary.Burns: Skin and tissue damage from heat, chemicals or electricity, causing large fluid losses.
glossary.Net water deficit: More water lost from the body than taken in.
glossary.Reabsorption: Kidney taking substances back from urine into the blood.
glossary.Passively: Moving without energy use, following a concentration gradient.
glossary.Pre-renal: Kidney injury caused by poor blood flow to the kidneys, not damage within them.
glossary.Volume-depleted: Having too little fluid in the circulation.
glossary.Organ perfusion: Blood flow delivering oxygen to the organs.
glossary.Hypernatraemic dehydration: Dehydration with high sodium because more water than salt has been lost.
glossary.Underlying cause: The disease or problem that led to the dehydration.
glossary.Low-volume urine: Passing small amounts of urine as the kidneys conserve water.
